decisions.statement: A call here is one bash call an agent made.
A call naming no argument reads the past twenty-four hours.
The rows are read from beside the page of the seat the call was made from.
Every seat is reached through the index rather than a folder named here.
Every numbered file of those rows is read rather than the first alone.
A row beside the same page spelling another phase counts nowhere here.
The runs are gathered under the opening of the first line the agent wrote.
A first line past the width a column holds is shortened to that width.
Two calls opening their first line alike are gathered as one row.
A row is written by the wrapper the weighing hook reads into a call.
The processor time recorded is what the call's children spent and so the call's.
A run that noted no high-water mark is left out of the memory reported.
A file that would not read is named rather than counting as no runs.
A row a write left half appended is passed over and the rest of the file read.
A first line holding no run of what was chosen is not listed at all.
The total counts the distinct runs read rather than the records read.
The total shares the processor time over the distinct runs read.
The total draws its average memory as `-`.
Calls are ordered by what their runs took on average.
Calls taking equal processor time are ordered by name.
A row here records no refusal.
A run writes no value the commit has.
Nothing here makes a call.
An argument this command does not take is refused.

definition: the command saying what a bash call cost in processor time and memory
